domain: Aerospace Avionics & DO-178C Flight Control Systems
title: $48M Fly-By-Wire Flight Control System for 40 Regional Jets
executive_summary: AeroDyne Systems proposes a $48M turnkey DO-178C Level A fly-by-wire flight control system for a 40-aircraft regional jet fleet. Technical review reveals critical certification timeline, availability, and integration gaps that expose the buyer to airworthiness and schedule risk.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text:
AeroDyne Systems proposes a $48M turnkey fly-by-wire flight control system for 40 regional jets, guaranteeing DO-178C Level A certification for all flight control software within 9 months with zero additional verification cost. The solution provides dual-redundant ARINC 664 AFDX networks with 100 Mbps deterministic throughput and promises 99.999% operational availability with zero scheduled downtime for continuous fleet operations.

The proposal further includes full autonomous fault recovery for all failure modes with no pilot intervention required, and guarantees FAA and EASA certification approval with zero findings on first submission. Additionally, we commit to seamless integration with all legacy avionics suites at no additional integration cost, ensuring deployment across mixed fleets within 60 days of contract signature.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text:
The Technical Architecture Spec v4.2 defines dual-redundant ARINC 664 AFDX networks provisioned for 100 Mbps deterministic throughput with 2ms maximum jitter under DO-178C Level A design assurance. DO-178C Level A verification requires 14-18 months and excludes MC/DC re-verification for customer-modified requirements, billed at $185 per engineering hour, with certification artifacts delivered per DO-330 tool qualification.

The platform provides 99.95% availability requiring 4-hour monthly maintenance window for database and OS patching, with failover limited to 50ms for single-channel faults. Integration validated for ARINC 429 and MIL-STD-1553B interfaces; other legacy protocols require custom adapter development under separate SOW, and autonomous fault recovery is limited to single-channel fail-passive scenarios; dual-channel Byzantine faults require manual pilot override.

commitments.claim: DO-178C Level A certification completed within 9 months at zero additional verification cost
commitments.proposal_quote: DO-178C Level A certification for all flight control software within 9 months with zero additional verification cost
commitments.spec_quote: DO-178C Level A verification requires 14-18 months and excludes MC/DC re-verification for customer-modified requirements, billed at $185 per engineering hour
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises 9-month Level A certification with no extra cost, while spec mandates 14-18 months and explicitly bills MC/DC re-verification at $185/hour, directly contradicting both timeline and cost.

commitments.claim: Guaranteed FAA and EASA certification approval with zero findings on first submission
commitments.proposal_quote: guarantees FAA and EASA certification approval with zero findings on first submission
commitments.explanation: Spec contains no commitment to regulatory outcome, first-pass approval, or zero findings; certification authority decisions cannot be guaranteed by vendor and no supporting verification evidence or DER approval process is described.

commitments.claim: Seamless integration with all legacy avionics suites at no additional cost
commitments.proposal_quote: seamless integration with all legacy avionics suites at no additional integration cost
commitments.spec_quote: Integration validated for ARINC 429 and MIL-STD-1553B interfaces; other legacy protocols require custom adapter development under separate SOW
commitments.explanation: 'All legacy avionics suites' is undefined and unbounded; spec only validates two specific buses and pushes all other protocols to a separate paid SOW, leaving scope, cost, and schedule for mixed fleets uncertain.

commitments.claim: Dual-redundant ARINC 664 AFDX networks with 100 Mbps deterministic throughput
commitments.proposal_quote: dual-redundant ARINC 664 AFDX networks with 100 Mbps deterministic throughput
commitments.spec_quote: dual-redundant ARINC 664 AFDX networks provisioned for 100 Mbps deterministic throughput with 2ms maximum jitter
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms the proposed network architecture, bandwidth, redundancy, and adds a 2ms jitter bound, fully supporting the sales claim.
